research_question: What is the main cause of packet loss in a multi-hop IoT network as network size and traffic load increase?
finding: Finding 1: Performance degrades as node count/traffic load increases
interpretation: Monotonic PDR decline with node count for all 3 protocols; throughput and delay trends corroborate a capacity/load effect, not a fixed reachability failure
limitation: AODV figures carry the FlowMonitor denominator caveat (indicative, not exact)

research_question: Can sigmoid-based adaptive routing (V4) improve delivery performance?
finding: Finding 2: V4 routing activation does not imply performance improvement
exact_result: Config 6 (x0_R=0.80,x0_L=0.50): 11/11 seeds re-route (100% activation), mean hop +27.9%, PDR change +3.5% (sign-test p=1.0, Cohen's d=+0.15, negative at median), delay +21.6% (d=+0.69), MaxLinkUtil +42.8%
interpretation: V4 demonstrably activates and restructures routes when tuned aggressively, but even the strongest-activation configuration produces no statistically credible delivery improvement and worsens latency/utilization
limitation: Only one network condition (N=50/medium/static) tested for activation; load term (x0_L sensitivity) never usefully engaged in the 27-config sensitivity sweep; broader traffic/topology sensitivity of activation is untested

research_question: Where does the dominant, measurable packet-loss mechanism occur?
finding: Finding 3: Gateway/first-hop congestion is the dominant measurable bottleneck under near-saturation
exact_result: Gateway airtime 0.86-0.89 at N>=75/high traffic; MAC-queue drops 1.2-2.4x over-represented at hop<=1 (concentration ratio); no secondary spatial hotspot (angular residual check, spread <=7%); NO_ROUTE/ROUTE_ERROR <2% of loss in every cell
interpretation: Airtime saturation and MAC-queue overflow concentrate at the gateway/1-hop ring; routing failure is ruled out as a material contributor
limitation: Only 0-53% of actual packet loss (txPkts-rxPkts) is attributable to any logged terminal-drop counter, even at the most saturated cell -- localization of the residual is inferred (structural/circumstantial), not directly measured

research_question: Is MAC-layer retry exhaustion the dominant loss mechanism?
finding: Finding 4: Retry exhaustion exists but is not the dominant measured mechanism
exact_result: Retry exhaustion accounts for 1.5-18.0% of loss per cell (mean ~6%); MAC-queue overflow larger in 10/12 cells (up to 53% of loss); retry drops concentrated at OUTER hops (hop2/hop3), airtime-negatively-correlated (r=-0.10 to -0.82 for OLSR) -- opposite spatial signature from queue overflow
interpretation: Retry exhaustion is real, measured directly (ns-3 MacTxFinalDataFailed trace) and distance/link-margin-driven, not contention-driven; it is a secondary, not dominant, mechanism
limitation: Residual unattributed loss (42-98%) persists even after adding this measurement -- the M2 decision is 'confirmed but not dominant', not 'fully explains loss'

research_question: Can the identified bottleneck be mitigated by reducing offered traffic rate?
finding: Finding 5: Offered-rate reduction improves OLSR PDR at N=75 and N=100
exact_result: OLSR N=75: PDR +14.7pp (26.28%->40.95%) at 4kbps vs 16kbps, monotonic in 6/6 individual seed-series; OLSR N=100: PDR +25.2pp (14.53%->39.74%), also monotonic in 6/6 seeds; OLSR N=100 throughput RISES at 12kbps (+25.5%) and 8kbps (+6.2%) despite less being offered
interpretation: Congestion relief (airtime -41% to -75%, MAC-queue drops -96% to -100%) translates into a genuine, seed-consistent delivery and (at N=100) capacity-recovery improvement for OLSR under near-saturated conditions
limitation: Effect is weak/mixed for OLSR at N=50 (not deeply saturated to begin with, baseline airtime 0.766 < the ~0.85 empirical reference); MaxRetryDrops does not monotonically decrease (increases at intermediate rate cuts before falling) -- one mechanism-chain link is inconsistent even where the outcome succeeds

research_question: Does the intervention work uniformly across protocols/conditions?
finding: Finding 6: Static/N=50 does not show the same improvement
exact_result: Static/N=50: PDR change -12.4pp(12kbps) to -2.7pp(4kbps) vs baseline (16kbps is the highest-PDR condition of the 4 tested); 7/9 individual Static seed-series across N=50/75/100 classified 'not-improving'; PDR seed CV 1.9-10.4% (low noise, rules out seed variability)
interpretation: Congestion-relief mechanism (airtime, MAC-queue drops) is measured and works identically for Static, but does not translate into a PDR benefit -- protocol/node-dependent outcome, not a universal intervention effect
limitation: Effect confirmed absent specifically at N=50 for Static (and weakly at N=50 for OLSR too) -- broader Static N=75/100 divergence from OLSR is noted but this diagnostic was scoped to N=50 only
thesis_section: Chapter 4 (Results) / Chapter 5 (Discussion) - limits of the intervention

research_question: Why does Static/N=50 not respond, and can the residual loss mechanism be identified?
finding: Finding 7: Residual packet loss remains partly unexplained by current instrumentation
exact_result: Known/attributed loss mechanisms (verified mutually exclusive from instrumentation definitions) explain 0.43-35.35% of total loss across the 12 runs (typically <2% once congestion is relieved); residual is 64.65-99.57% of loss, >=92% in 10/12 runs, at every rate level including baseline
interpretation: Congestion relief occurred but the relieved mechanisms were never the dominant loss source for Static/N=50 -- explains the null PDR result quantitatively without inventing a specific physical cause for the residual
limitation: The specific identity of the residual mechanism (PHY collision vs. another cause) is explicitly NOT determined; PHY RX-drop event volume is the largest circumstantial signal but is not confirmable as 1:1 with final loss (per the M2 finding)
